findings.title: main() ends by closing THEIR client and, with a GUI, stepping the sim for 4 s; the readback at main() return and the G6 step count do not account for it
findings.plan_location: D2, D3, G6 (readback at main() return, stepSimulation outside main()), B2 env_adapter override list, B3(c), B7 GUI twin
findings.problem: main() finishes with an epilogue the plan never mentions. With gui set it runs env.step_simulation() in a loop for 4 s (about 960 steps at 240 Hz) after the last dispatched action, and it always ends with env.close(). BoxelTestEnv.close() disconnects self.client_id and the plan client; in the bridge client_id is the adopted client 0, their executing world. D2/D3/G6 put the scoring readback after main() returns (execute_fn returns the D3 observation), and G6 wants an arm readback at main() return plus a second one at observation build. As written neither readback can be taken, and their own env.step (steps 1..19, deep copies, pickling) would face a dead client. B2 lists only two overrides (oracle_detect_objects, update_object_positions) and B3(c) has no epilogue switch, so the harness needs an unregistered patch. Honesty angle: the 4 s GUI loop is stepSimulation inside main(), so G6's 'outside main()' count is blind to it while the last POSITION_CONTROL targets keep driving the arm toward home, i.e. exactly the post-hoc settle toward the 1e-4 at-home boundary that R3.7 closed for the headless path. B7's watched episodes run with the GUI, so their at-home outcome can differ from the headless twin with no gate firing.
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:2353-2358 (gui hold: env.step_simulation() for 4 s), :2362 (env.close()); boxel_env.py:1898-1907 (close disconnects client_id and plan_client_id); plan G6 lines 144-148, D2 lines 428-432, B2 lines 755-763.
findings.required_change: Pre-register in B3(c), default byte-identical, an epilogue switch for main(): no GUI hold and no env.close() on the bridge path (or an adapter close() that leaves client 0 connected and closes only the plan twin), and take the first G6 readback inside that return path. State that G6 counts stepSimulation on the executing client between the last dispatched action and the observation build in GUI and headless runs alike, and that B7's GUI twin uses the same switch.

findings.title: D7 (vii) leaves the final-hold step cap and convergence rule unregistered, although it alone decides whether the strict at-home test can pass
findings.plan_location: D7 (v)-(vii), B1(i), D8 constant list, B6, G9, R3
findings.problem: move_robot_smooth's endpoint settle stops at 2e-3 rad after at most 120 steps, twenty times their tolerance, so a corrective move planned from q_readback_k repeats the same miss and home_not_reached fires; only the new hold (converge to np.allclose 1e-4, or a bounded step cap) can make the headline strict test passable. The text fixes neither the cap value, nor the convergence criterion (all 7 joints, which norm), nor any rule mapping B1(i)'s measurements to the cap. D8's list of task-spec constants and B6's freeze do not contain it, and G9 names no source for it. The number 'two' in home_not_reached is registered; the cap is not. A cap chosen after B7 shows at-home misses is the outcome-fitted tolerance rule that R3 says must never happen, and nothing in the plan would detect it. The plan also gives no branch for B1(i) showing the 1e-4 test unreachable with the die payload (D11 has such a branch for grasp width).
findings.evidence: robot_utils.py:775-788 (existing hold: 120-step cap, 2e-3 tolerance), test_full_pipeline.py:1583-1585 (settle only on the final waypoint); plan D7 lines 575-578, B1(i) lines 738-741, D8 lines 587-606, G9 lines 172-178.
findings.required_change: Pre-register the cap and criterion now as a stated function of B1(i) (for example 2x the maximum steps B1(i) needs to reach np.allclose(readback, q_home, 1e-4, 1e-4) over its grid, empty-handed and with the die-mass payload), add it to D8's list and to B6's single BF#, and add a D11-style branch: if B1(i) shows the strict test unreachable, the headline stays strict, the report says 0 by construction, and the user decides; no tolerance is relaxed.

findings.title: The G1/G3/G14 trap lists still omit calls that roll back the world or advance physics without a stepSimulation call
findings.problem: v4 extended the lists with the calls R3.8 named, but they remain enumerations. Not covered: restoreState (with saveState as its enabler), which rolls back every body and the robot and is a free retry; loadBullet, loadSDF, loadMJCF; resetSimulation, reachable through the adapter's inherited BoxelTestEnv.reset(); and setRealTimeSimulation, which in GUI mode makes the server step physics with no stepSimulation call, so G6's zero-step count and the G3 hook are both blind to it. Each would pass G1, G3, G14 and G21. The main-pipeline modules use none of them on the adopt path (resetSimulation only at construction and reset), so no allowlist entry is needed and the omission costs nothing to close.
findings.evidence: plan G1 lines 81-94, G3 lines 110-122, G14 lines 214-232; boxel_env.py:510, 525 (construction), 1877-1890 (reset() with resetSimulation and setRealTimeSimulation(0) at :1890); grep of execution.py, test_full_pipeline.py, robot_utils.py, streams.py, perception.py, world_eye.py, telemetry.py finds no saveState/restoreState/loadBullet.
findings.required_change: Add saveState, restoreState, loadBullet, loadSDF, loadMJCF, loadSoftBody, resetSimulation to G1's grep and to G14's executing-client trap, trap setRealTimeSimulation with any value other than 0, and assert that the adapter's reset() raises. Phrase G1/G14 as 'every pybullet call that writes world or robot state' with the grep list as its current instance.

findings.title: D6's 'last imaged' record, the sole justification for a not_here interior with no render of its grid, has no defined mechanism
findings.plan_location: D6 STATUS RULE, G5 channel 'observed before placement', B5 deliverable and effort
findings.problem: R3.10 resolved the two W definitions by saying the 'record of when each cell was last imaged supplies the observational part'. D6 then defines free cells as 'the complement of the registered OBJECT and SHADOW regions inside W'. Nothing says what a cell is, which renders stamp it, whether a cell behind the arm or inside a shadow at that render counts as imaged, where the record is stored, or when it is invalidated. B5's deliverable lists region_kind, interior_boxel_ids and 'the D6 status rule' but no record, and its 3-5 day estimate does not price one. This record is the only thing between M2 and the archived 'cups already moved are empty' bookkeeping that D6 REJECTS: an implementer can satisfy the rule by testing the destination against the current registry complement ('nothing is registered there'), which is that bookkeeping under another name, and G5 cannot tell the difference because it only requires that a provenance row exists. A not_here write without a render of the region's grid is the one belief write in the plan that H3 and the LW1 door cannot audit.
findings.evidence: plan D6 lines 521-539, G5 lines 125-138, B5 lines 857-888; archived per-cup bookkeeping cited at boxel_policy.py:352-353 (plan lines 137-138, 544).
findings.required_change: Define the record in B5: grid and cell size, the stamping rule (a cell is stamped free only when a render shows its column unoccluded by any body including the arm, and stamped occupied otherwise), invalidation on any later registration, move or place, storage in the ledger. Make the G5 row carry the stamp times of the cells it rests on. Add a negative test: a cup placed on cells that were arm-occluded at their last render must create an unknown interior.

findings.title: G1 greps all of tampura_bridge/ including tests/, but the G6 controls in B0 need teleports and fault injection
findings.plan_location: G1 scope, G6 positive and negative controls, B0
findings.problem: G1 is a weld/teleport grep 'over tampura_bridge/'. B0 puts the G6 controls in pytest cases 'under tampura_bridge/tests/'. A positive control needs a verified two-pad hold of the die with the arm at DEFAULT_ARM_POS, which requires resetJointState/resetBasePositionAndOrientation (or equivalent) to build, and the fault injections (go_home no_path, a failed lift, a slip) need monkeypatching or a forced reset. Either G1 is red on the package's own tests, or tests/ is silently excluded, which is an unregistered scope decision that also removes a directory from a cheat gate.
findings.evidence: plan G1 line 81, G6 lines 139-150, B0 lines 694-703.
findings.required_change: State the scope: G1 and G7 run over the campaign import graph rooted at run_bridge_on_finddice.py; tampura_bridge/tests/ is excluded, imported by nothing on that graph (asserted by an import-graph check), and the controls' set-up calls live in one reviewed allowlist file.

findings.title: D7 (iii)-(iv) say the move to q_home is planned with the die as cargo; the code does not do that for the first move after the pick
findings.plan_location: D7 (iii) and (iv), R3.1 integration, B3 test list
findings.problem: D7 (iii) says move can reach q_home 'through plan-motion with the die as cargo' and (iv) says the post-pick and readback configurations carry held_body_ids. In the plan [pick die, move q_kin -> q_home], q1 is the planner's compute-kin config, whose metadata is only ignored_body_ids={die} and grasp_ee_offset; held_body_ids is set only by compute_stack_kin. plan_motion then takes held = q1.ignored & q2.ignored = {} because q_home ignores nothing, and the runtime re-solve copies q1.held_body_ids (empty) from the plan's q1, not from current_config. So the transit home is checked empty-handed, with is_pick_place true (whole-path gripper-collision relaxation), and (iv) only helps a corrective move planned in a LATER plan, where current_config is q1. The die rides physically with the gripper through a twin that does not model it; a swept cup or a failed transit then triggers the integrity replan, and the pressure to patch it with a bridge-side rule (the scripted-motion pattern R7 forbids) is the same as for R3.1.
findings.evidence: streams.py:934-937 (held = intersection of ignored sets when neither endpoint declares held), :1434-1435 (compute-kin sets ignored and grasp_ee_offset only), :1586 (only compute_stack_kin sets held_body_ids); test_full_pipeline.py:1520, 1541-1547 (q1_runtime built from the plan's q1), :1594-1597 (readback carries joints and name only); plan D7 lines 556-565.
findings.required_change: Either correct D7 to say the first post-pick transit is planned and re-solved with the die ignored but not carried, add the sweep risk to the P4.6 disclosures, and keep (iv) for corrective moves only; or pre-register in B3(d), default off, that the move handler's runtime re-solve carries the dispatcher's held body (held_body_ids and the grasp offset from held_body_id), with a B3 test that a post-pick move to q_home is re-solved with the die as cargo. Do not set held_body_ids on compute-kin configs: that would make the approach to the pick treat the die as already held.
